instruction:
Please act as a professional Verilog designer. Your task is to create a Verilog module that implements a multiplier circuit for both unsigned and signed numbers. 
The module should have the following inputs and outputs:

Inputs: two n-bit numbers (A and B) and a control signal (ctrl)
Outputs: an n-bit product (P)
The module should also have the following parameters:

n: the bit-width of the input and output signals
The multiplier should be able to perform both unsigned and signed multiplication, depending on the value of the control signal (ctrl). 

If ctrl is 0, the input numbers should be treated as unsigned, and the output should be the unsigned product of A and B. 
If ctrl is 1, the input numbers should be treated as signed two's complement numbers, and the output should be the signed product of A and B.

To implement the multiplier, you should first check the value of the control signal. 
If it is 0, you can simply use Verilog's "*" operator to compute the unsigned product of A and B. 
If it is 1, you will need to perform signed multiplication.

For signed multiplication, you should first check the sign bits of the input numbers. 
If they are both positive or both negative, you can use the "*" operator to compute the unsigned product of the absolute values of A and B, and then adjust the sign of the result based on the sign bits. 
If one of the numbers is negative, you will need to take the two's complement of that number before performing the multiplication.

Your module should be able to handle overflow and underflow conditions, and should produce correct results for all possible input combinations.
original_rtl:
module multiplier (
  input signed [n-1:0] A,
  input signed [n-1:0] B,
  input ctrl,
  output signed [n-1:0] P
);

parameter n = 8; // bit-width of input and output signals

reg signed [2*n-1:0] temp; // intermediate result for signed multiplication

always @(*) begin
  if (ctrl == 0) begin // unsigned multiplication
    P = A * B;
  end else begin // signed multiplication
    if (A[n-1] == B[n-1]) begin // both positive or both negative
      temp = A * B;
      if (temp[2*n-1] == 1) begin // overflow
        P = {1'b1, {n-1{1'b0}}}; // set to maximum signed value
      end else begin
        P = temp[n-1:0];
      end
    end else begin // one positive and one negative
      if (A[n-1] == 1) begin // A is negative
        temp = (~A + 1) * B;
      end else begin // B is negative
        temp = A * (~B + 1);
      end
      if (temp[2*n-1] == 1) begin // overflow
        P = {1'b1, {n-1{1'b0}}}; // set to maximum signed value
      end else begin
        P = ~temp[n-1:0] + 1; // two's complement to get signed result
      end
    end
  end
end

endmodule
